prompt.content:
You are analyzing the evaluation of one candidate change to a 3D-IC physical design flow.
Hypothesis of the change: c025's cap of 15.68 is the strongest robust parent (robust +0.254, min +0.245); a modest x0.5 tightening to 7.84 was already tried (c024), so instead I fine-tune the *other* coefficient in the same mechanism — the momentum decay clamp — from 0.5 to 0.25 (x0.5), which makes the criticality signal even more responsive to the current placement so many moderately-critical nets keep weight (TNS) while the per-net cap stays at c025's proven 15.68.
Rule-based digest:
total=+0.774 robust(mean-std)=+0.215 min_case=+0.205 all_valid=True
  ariane133-ng45: score=+0.311 dWNS=+14.4% dTNS=+42.3% overflow~82
  bp-ng45: score=+0.258 dWNS=+15.0% dTNS=+32.9% overflow~105
  bp_fe-ng45: score=+0.205 dWNS=+8.5% dTNS=+28.6% overflow~148
Write <=120 words. If some runs are INVALID (failures listed), first say what kind of failure it is (legality / crash / timeout) and whether it looks systematic (all seeds of a case) or sporadic - an invalid candidate says nothing about the hypothesis itself; suggest how to make the same idea legal. Otherwise: (1) did the hypothesis hold? (2) which case/metric moved and plausible mechanism, (3) one concrete next-step suggestion. No preamble.

response: The hypothesis held: tightening the momentum decay clamp to 0.25 while keeping c025's 15.68 cap improved all three cases (total +0.774, robust +0.215, min +0.205, all valid). Gains concentrate in dTNS (+28–42%) with smaller dWNS (+8–15%), consistent with the mechanism—more responsive criticality keeps moderately-critical nets weighted, improving TNS. Overflow rises modestly (~82–148). Next step: sweep the decay clamp between 0.25 and 0.5 (e.g., 0.35) to check for a monotonic trend and confirm 0.25 isn't past the optimum.
